chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Muhammad ibn Sinan said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the one whom a person catches, then he has caught the Hajj. He said: 'If he arrives at Jam' while the people are at al-Mash'ar al-Haram before the sunrise, then he has caught the Hajj and his Umrah is not valid. And if he catches Jam' after the sunrise, it is a separate Umrah and he has no Hajj. If he wishes to stay in Mecca, he stays; and if he wishes to return to his family, he returns, and Hajj is incumbent upon him next year.'

key_terms.الْمَشْعَرِ الْحَرَام: Al-Mash'ar al-Haram, the sacred monument/mass gathering place
key_terms.جَمْع: Jam', the station near Mecca where pilgrims gather
key_terms.عُمْرَةٌ مُفْرَدَة: Umrah al-Mufradah, a standalone Umrah distinct from Hajj

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who arrives at Jam' after sunrise?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Rida (AS), the criterion for valid Hajj is strictly tied to the timing of the stay at Muzdalifah (Jam') before sunrise; arriving late invalidates the Hajj pillar, reducing it to a standalone Umrah. This ruling highlights the Shia emphasis on the specific temporal conditions of ritual acts, distinguishing between the obligatory Hajj and the voluntary Umrah, while offering flexibility for the pilgrim to either remain in Mecca or return home with the obligation to perform Hajj the following year.
